Apple___Apple_scab.description: A fungal disease caused by Venturia inaequalis that affects apple leaves and fruit, creating dark, scabby lesions.
Apple___Apple_scab.solution: Prune and remove infected leaves and fruits. Apply fungicides containing captan, mancozeb, or sulfur at early growth stages.

Apple___Black_rot.description: Caused by the fungus Botryosphaeria obtusa, this disease leads to rotting fruit and cankers on twigs and branches.
Apple___Black_rot.solution: Remove infected fruit and twigs. Apply copper-based fungicides during early spring.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.description: A fungal infection that causes yellow-orange spots on leaves, transmitted between apple and cedar trees.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.solution: Remove nearby cedar trees if possible. Use fungicides like myclobutanil or propiconazole early in the season.

Apple___healthy.description: Apple plant appears healthy with no visible disease symptoms.
Apple___healthy.solution: Maintain regular pruning, watering, and balanced fertilization to ensure long-term health.

Blueberry___healthy.description: No visible signs of disease on the blueberry plant.
Blueberry___healthy.solution: Maintain acidic soil (pH 4.5–5.5), proper mulching, and watering.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.description: Cherry plant shows healthy growth without infection.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.solution: Ensure good drainage and avoid overhead watering to prevent fungal growth.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.description: Fungal infection causing white powdery growth on leaves and fruits.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.solution: Apply sulfur or neem oil sprays. Improve air circulation by pruning dense branches.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.description: Caused by Cercospora species, it forms rectangular gray lesions on leaves reducing photosynthesis.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.solution: Use resistant hybrids, rotate crops, and apply strobilurin fungicides.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: Fungal infection that produces reddish-brown pustules on corn leaves.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.solution: Plant resistant varieties and apply fungicides like tebuconazole or azoxystrobin.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.description: Corn plant is healthy with green leaves and no infection.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.solution: Maintain proper spacing and nitrogen levels to avoid diseases.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.description: Caused by Exserohilum turcicum fungus, leading to long, elliptical gray-green lesions.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.solution: Use resistant varieties and practice crop rotation. Apply fungicides at early tasseling.

Grape___Black_rot.description: A fungal disease that causes black lesions on leaves and rotting of grapes.
Grape___Black_rot.solution: Remove mummified fruit and prune infected vines. Apply mancozeb or myclobutanil sprays.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).description: A complex disease affecting grapevine wood, causing tiger-striped leaves and black spots on fruit.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).solution: Remove infected vines and avoid pruning during wet weather. Apply sodium arsenite substitutes where allowed.

Grape___healthy.description: Healthy grapevine without signs of disease.
Grape___healthy.solution: Maintain balanced irrigation and proper pruning for airflow.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.description: Fungal leaf disease causing angular brown spots leading to defoliation.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.solution: Spray with fungicides like chlorothalonil or copper oxychloride.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).description: Serious bacterial disease caused by Candidatus Liberibacter species, spread by psyllid insects.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).solution: Remove and destroy infected trees. Control psyllids with imidacloprid. Use disease-free saplings.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.description: Caused by Xanthomonas campestris, leading to dark spots on leaves and fruits.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.solution: Apply copper sprays. Avoid overhead watering and prune infected branches.

Peach___healthy.description: Peach plant shows healthy leaves and fruits.
Peach___healthy.solution: Ensure proper irrigation, pruning, and balanced fertilization.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.description: Caused by Xanthomonas species, creating small, dark, water-soaked spots on leaves.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.solution: Use disease-free seeds and apply copper-based fungicides.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.description: Bell pepper plant is healthy and disease-free.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.solution: Maintain crop rotation and avoid wet leaf surfaces.

Potato___Early_blight.description: Caused by Alternaria solani, resulting in concentric dark rings on leaves.
Potato___Early_blight.solution: Apply fungicides like mancozeb or chlorothalonil and remove infected leaves.

Potato___healthy.description: Potato plant with green, intact leaves and no disease symptoms.
Potato___healthy.solution: Avoid waterlogging and maintain soil health with compost or organic matter.

Potato___Late_blight.description: Caused by Phytophthora infestans, the same pathogen behind the Irish potato famine, leading to leaf rot.
Potato___Late_blight.solution: Apply fungicides like metalaxyl or cymoxanil. Avoid overhead watering.

Raspberry___healthy.description: Raspberry plant appears healthy and vigorous.
Raspberry___healthy.solution: Keep rows weed-free and ensure good airflow to prevent fungal issues.

Soybean___healthy.description: Soybean plant shows no signs of fungal or bacterial infection.
Soybean___healthy.solution: Rotate crops annually and monitor for rust or blight symptoms.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.description: White powdery fungus covering leaves, reducing photosynthesis.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.solution: Apply sulfur dust or potassium bicarbonate sprays and increase spacing.

Strawberry___healthy.description: Strawberry plant is free from fungal or bacterial infections.
Strawberry___healthy.solution: Avoid excessive moisture and remove old mulch after harvest.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.description: Fungal infection causing reddish-purple spots that merge and dry leaf margins.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.solution: Use fungicides like captan and remove old leaves after fruiting.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: Caused by Xanthomonas campestris, this leads to small, dark leaf spots and fruit blemishes.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.solution: Use copper-based sprays and avoid working with wet plants.

Tomato___Early_blight.description: Fungal disease caused by Alternaria solani, causing concentric brown leaf spots.
Tomato___Early_blight.solution: Apply fungicides regularly and rotate crops every 2–3 years.

Tomato___healthy.description: Tomato plant is healthy and free from visible infections.
Tomato___healthy.solution: Provide balanced fertilizer, adequate sunlight, and watering at the base.

Tomato___Late_blight.description: Caused by Phytophthora infestans, leading to rapid leaf decay and fruit rot.
Tomato___Late_blight.solution: Use resistant varieties and spray fungicides containing chlorothalonil or copper sulfate.
